newsitem.title: USA: U.S. presses Japan on N. Korea aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. presses Japan on N. Korea aid.

text.p: The United States urged Japan on Thursday to provide food aid to famine-threatened North Korea and said this issue woud be raised when Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto visits Washington on Friday.

"We believe there's a severe food shortage in North Korea," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said when asked about Japanese reluctance to donate. "We believe that it is an international humanitarian imperative to meet that food shortage. And we call upon all countries to contribute."

Japan's top government spokesman said on Tuesday that Tokyo may not give food aid to North Korea because of a big drug seizure aboard a North Korean freighter and suspicions over kidnapped Japanese nationals.
After some scepticism, the United States has become an advocate of more aid to ease North Korea's severe food shortages, worsened by two years of flooding.
Washington pledged $25 million in response to recent U.N. World Food Programme appeals for $95.5 million in food aid for North Korea.

While urging Japan to provide aid, the United States on Thursday reaffirmed its rejection of North Korean demands for large-scale food aid, a lifting of U.S. trade sanctions and diplomatic recognition as preconditions for entering into Korean peninsula peace talks. The talks should not be tied to food aid, the State Department said.
